newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO MANGO PRODUCERS TO LAUNCH GLOBAL CAMPAIGN.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO MANGO PRODUCERS TO LAUNCH GLOBAL CAMPAIGN.

text.p: Mexican mango producers and the country's foreign trade bank Bancomext said on Wednesday they were about to launch a $4 million campaign to promote the tropical fruit worldwide.
"It is more than just advertising, it is marketing in general to promote mangoes abroad," Bancomext official Enrique Vilatela told reporters.
He said the bank and the mango producers would contribute equal parts to a $4 million fund that would be used for advertising and to consolidate international markets.
Mexican mangoes are mainly exported to the United States and Canada, but the producers would like to increase their currently small European market share.
Mexico is the world's second-largest producer of mangoes after India, producing 1.4 million tonnes in 1996.
In 1993 Mexico exported 23.4 million cases weighing on average 4.5 kilograms. This grew to 36.8 million cases in 1996.

Statistics from Mexico's Association of Mango Packers show Mexico is likely to earn $117.2 million from mango exports to the United States this year, and $139.6 through sales to the rest of the world.
Emex president Luis Villegas said the group would develop the international promotion strategy in conjunction with Bancomext in September.
The campaign is expected to last five to six months until the next season begins in March. ((--Monica Ballesca, Guadelajara newsroom +523 817-0397))
